summary: Feng Youlan worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Columbia University. He held posts at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1946–1947).

Ferdinand Christian Baur was a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and the Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814), and later held a post at the University of Tübingen from ~1826 to 1860.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829) and held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Marburg, where he later served as professor and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing worked in sinology, tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1905). His career included teaching posts at Peking University (1919–1921), Humboldt University (~1927–1938), and the University of California, Berkeley (1938).

Ferdinand Sommer specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Marburg, Freiberg, and Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen, habilitating at Leipzig. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Geneva, Berlin, EPHE, the Sorbonne, and Leipzig. He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and University of Paris (1881–1891), and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
Ferdinand von Eckstein was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Friedrich Creuzer. He founded Le Catholique in 1826 and was a member of the Société Asiatique (~1823–1861).
Ferenc Ruzsa works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he took up a post in ~1989.
Fernand Meyer is a scholar in Tibetology. He has held positions at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University under the doctoral supervision of Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1934–1945) and held posts at the University of Buenos Aires, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).
Filippo De Filippi was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

Filippo Marsili is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà. He has held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Michael Witzel and Masato Fujii, and later held positions at Yale University (2017–2018) and Brown University (attested 2020).

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard, he held positions at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1850), Sanskrit College and University (1853), King's College London (1862), and the India Office (~1862–1869).

Flavio Geisshuesler works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Bern, Lausanne, and the University of Virginia under David Germano, holding posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) and the University of Sydney (attested 2026).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking, and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His posts include Kansai Medical University (1994–2001), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin (~2009–2013). She has held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies (2013), the University of Hamburg (~2015–2016), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2016).
